holidays.name: National Onion Rings Day
holidays.description: A crunchy, golden-brown salute to the humble onion, battered, fried, and stacked on a finger like jewelry. Celebrate by ordering a tower of rings, dunking them in your favorite sauce, and pretending the grease counts as a vegetable serving.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American food holiday, widely listed on food-observance calendars. Its exact founder is unclear, but it joined the crowded lineup of fried-food celebrations that spread through restaurants and social media.
holidays.funFact: Onion rings appeared in an 1802 cookbook by British author John Mollard, who described slicing onions, dipping them in batter, and frying them, long before drive-ins made them famous.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Eclair Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the elegant, cream-filled pastry that makes fancy bakeries feel like French vacations. Whether you like classic chocolate glaze or a wild modern flavor, today is a license to eat dessert with a fork or, more bravely, with your hands.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance celebrating the French pastry, whose name means 'flash of lightning' in French. The eclair itself dates to 19th-century France, and the holiday is a modern food-calendar addition.
holidays.funFact: The word eclair means 'lightning' in French, with the popular theory being that the pastry is eaten so fast it disappears in a flash.

holidays.name: Take Your Dog to Work Day
holidays.description: A day when offices are invited to become part dog park, part conference room. Coworkers get furry colleagues, meetings get adorable interruptions, and productivity may or may not survive the belly rubs.
holidays.origin: Created in 1996 by Pet Sitters International to celebrate the companionship of dogs and encourage adoption. It is traditionally held on the Friday following Father's Day in the United States, so the date moves, but it often falls around this time in June.
holidays.funFact: The event was launched by Pet Sitters International in 1996, and the group says it hopes the day also boosts adoptions from shelters by showing coworkers how great dogs are.

holidays.name: World Rainforest Day
holidays.description: A leafy, humid celebration of the planet's wettest wonderlands, home to more species than anyone has managed to count. People mark it by learning about rainforest wildlife, supporting conservation groups, or just yelling 'canopy!' at a houseplant.
holidays.origin: Founded in 2017 by the Rainforest Partnership, a nonprofit, and observed each June 22 to raise awareness about deforestation and promote protecting forests worldwide.
holidays.funFact: Rainforests cover only about 6 percent of Earth's land surface, yet they are believed to house more than half of the world's plant and animal species.

holidays.name: National Pecan Sandies Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the buttery, crumbly, nut-studded shortbread cookie that tastes like a cozy grandma kitchen. It is the perfect excuse to pair a cookie with milk, coffee, or both, and to defend your right to eat them dunked.
holidays.origin: An unofficial cookie holiday popularized through food-day calendars. The sandy texture of the cookie is what inspired the name, rather than any beach connection.
holidays.funFact: Pecan sandies get their name from their sandy, crumbly texture, and the cookie is a close relative of Scottish shortbread.
